course.title: AP World History: Modern
course.description: Understand the people, ideas, and connections that shaped the world from c. 1200 to the present.
course.previewDescription: Explore how states rose, belief systems spread, trade networks connected regions, and revolutions reshaped societies from c. 1200 to the present.

unit.title: Transoceanic Interconnections
unit.description: Study how new maritime technology, state-sponsored voyages, the Columbian Exchange, and coerced labor connected the world's oceans and reshaped societies.

themes.title: Interactions of humans with the environment
themes.question: How did geography, crops, resources, or disease shape choices?
themes.example: Andean terraces made steep slopes more usable for farming.

themes.title: Social interactions and organization
themes.question: Who had status, opportunities, or obligations?
themes.example: Examination preparation favored families that could afford education.

themes.title: Political systems and governance
themes.question: How did rulers gain authority and administer territory?
themes.example: Song officials carried imperial decisions into local government.

themes.title: Economic systems
themes.question: How were goods produced, exchanged, taxed, or distributed?
themes.example: Mali drew revenue from commerce through its territory.

themes.title: Cultural developments and interactions
themes.question: How did beliefs, learning, and artistic practices influence society?
themes.example: Buddhist monasteries connected religious practice with education.

themes.title: Technology and innovation
themes.question: What techniques or tools changed what people could do?
themes.example: Inca roads and knotted records helped officials coordinate resources.

questions.prompt: The Portuguese empire in the Indian Ocean is best described as
choices: a network of ports granted to Portugal by the Mughal emperor in a formal treaty
a merchant community with no armed forces
a network of fortified ports that taxed and controlled sea trade
a territorial empire that ruled most of India
questions.explanation: Portugal held fortified ports such as Goa and Malacca and forced ships to buy passes.
choiceExplanations: Portugal captured ports such as Goa by force.
Portugal used armed ships to enforce its system.
Portugal held fortified ports such as Goa and Malacca and forced ships to buy passes.
Portugal never ruled most of India.
questions.distinguisher: Ports were the basis, but Portugal seized them by force rather than receiving them from the Mughals.

questions.prompt: Joint-stock companies such as the VOC helped European expansion mainly by
choices: replacing state involvement in overseas trade entirely
allowing Asian rulers to buy shares and control European trade
spreading risks among investors while banning the use of force against rivals
spreading the risks and costs of long voyages among many investors
questions.explanation: Selling shares spread costs and risks, making expensive voyages possible.
choiceExplanations: Governments chartered the companies and gave them special powers.
Shareholders were mainly European.
The VOC used force to control the spice trade.
Selling shares spread costs and risks, making expensive voyages possible.
questions.distinguisher: Risk sharing is right, but the companies were allowed to build forts and keep armies.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best explains the Spanish defeat of the Mexica Empire?
choices: Spanish steel weapons and guns alone, without help from any Indigenous allies

choiceExplanations: Indigenous allies and disease were essential.
Allies who resented Mexica rule, smallpox, and Spanish steel and guns combined to defeat the Mexica.
The Spanish were greatly outnumbered.

questions.prompt: The Asante kingdom grew powerful in the 1700s mainly by
choices: converting to Christianity under Portuguese pressure
trading gold for silver brought across the Atlantic from Spanish America
trading gold and enslaved captives for firearms and cloth
conquering Portuguese colonies in Brazil
questions.explanation: Asante rulers sold gold and war captives to Europeans and used firearms to expand.
choiceExplanations: Asante kept its own religion.
Asante's main imports were firearms and cloth.
Asante rulers sold gold and war captives to Europeans and used firearms to expand.

questions.prompt: Which of the following was a difference between Portuguese expansion in Asia and Spanish expansion in the Americas?
choices: Portugal controlled ports, while Spain conquered and governed large territories
Portugal conquered large empires, while Spain controlled only ports
Portugal relied on joint-stock companies, while Spain relied only on missionaries

questions.explanation: Portugal held coastal forts in Asia, while Spain built a territorial empire in the Americas.
choiceExplanations: Portugal held coastal forts in Asia, while Spain built a territorial empire in the Americas.
This reverses the two.
Portugal's Asian trade was a royal enterprise, and Spain used soldiers and officials, not only missionaries.

questions.prompt: Afonso I of Kongo's letters protesting Portuguese slave raiding are best used as evidence that
choices: African rulers sometimes tried to limit European demands
Kongo had no contact with Europe before 1700
Afonso opposed Christianity

questions.explanation: Afonso traded with Portugal but protested when its traders enslaved his subjects.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 4.4 key concept: Europeans established new trading posts in Africa and Asia, which proved profitable for the rulers and merchants involved in new global trade networks
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing the Portuguese trading-post empire, 1498–1600
stimulusBlocks.text:
The Portuguese did not conquer large territories in Asia. Instead they seized fortified ports at key points: Goa in India in 1510, Malacca in 1511, and Hormuz near the Persian Gulf. From these bases they required Asian merchant ships to buy a pass, the cartaz, and pay duties at Portuguese ports, or risk being attacked.

This system brought large profits but limited control. Most Indian Ocean trade continued to be carried by Asian merchants, and powerful land empires such as the Mughals were largely unaffected by Portuguese naval power.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes the author's view of the Portuguese system?
choices: It gave Portugal complete control of Asian trade
It failed to produce any profits
It was unprofitable but gave Portugal wide control
It was profitable, but its control was limited
questions.explanation: The author says it brought large profits but limited control.
choiceExplanations: Most trade stayed with Asian merchants.
It brought large profits.
It was profitable and its control was limited.
The author says it brought large profits but limited control.
questions.distinguisher: The author says most trade stayed in Asian hands, so control was far from complete.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, the VOC raised money for its voyages by
choices: borrowing silver from the Ming government
selling shares only to the Dutch royal family

collecting taxes from Dutch citizens

choiceExplanations: The Ming did not finance the VOC.
Many investors bought shares.
As a joint-stock company, the VOC sold shares to many investors.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 4.4 key concept: European merchants' role in Asian trade was characterized by joint-stock companies and by efforts to dominate trade in specific goods
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing the Dutch East India Company, 1602–1700
stimulusBlocks.text:
In 1602 the Dutch government chartered the Dutch East India Company, known by its Dutch initials VOC. As a joint-stock company, it raised money by selling shares to many investors, who shared the profits and the risks of long, dangerous voyages. The company could build forts, keep soldiers, and make treaties.

From its headquarters at Batavia on Java, founded in 1619, the VOC used force to control the trade in nutmeg, cloves, and mace. On the Banda Islands in the 1620s, company forces killed or enslaved much of the population and replaced them with plantations worked by enslaved laborers.

questions.prompt: The events on the Banda Islands described in the passage show that the VOC
choices: traded only through peaceful negotiation
worked mainly to spread Christianity
used violence only against European rivals
used violence to gain control of valuable goods
questions.explanation: Company forces killed or enslaved much of the population to control nutmeg.
choiceExplanations: The passage describes force.
The company's goal was profit.
Banda's own population was attacked.
Company forces killed or enslaved much of the population to control nutmeg.
questions.distinguisher: The VOC fought European rivals, but on Banda its violence fell on the islands' own people.

questions.prompt: The passage best supports which of the following claims about Afonso I of Kongo?
choices: He conquered Portuguese colonies in Brazil
He adopted Christianity and encouraged slave raiding in Kongo
He adopted Christianity but objected to Portuguese slave raiding
He refused all contact with Portugal
questions.explanation: He converted and exchanged ambassadors but protested the enslavement of his subjects.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 4.4 key concept: expansion of maritime trading networks fostered the growth of states in Africa, including the Asante and the Kingdom of the Kongo
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing how Kongo and Asante took part in Atlantic trade, c. 1490–1750
stimulusBlocks.text:
The Kingdom of Kongo in west-central Africa established relations with Portugal in the 1480s. King Afonso I, who ruled from about 1509 to 1542, converted to Christianity and exchanged ambassadors with Portugal, but he also wrote letters protesting that Portuguese traders were enslaving his subjects.

The Asante kingdom, which rose in the forests of present-day Ghana around 1700, grew powerful by selling gold and enslaved war captives to European traders on the coast in exchange for firearms and cloth. Its rulers used the firearms to expand their state.

questions.prompt: Kongo and Asante were similar in that both
choices: took part in trade with Europeans that affected their states
were conquered by Portugal in the 1500s
rejected all European goods
took part in European trade without any internal effects
questions.explanation: Both traded with Europeans, which shaped their power and societies.
choiceExplanations: Both traded with Europeans, which shaped their power and societies.
Neither was conquered in this way.
Both traded for European goods.
Trade had major effects in both states.
questions.distinguisher: Trade did affect both: Kongo lost subjects to slave raiding and Asante used firearms to expand.
